files.internal_title: Canada Pension Plan Contributions and Overpayment
files.note: Schedule 8, 5000-S8 E (25), T1-2025 — a CRA-issued fillable PDF (Designer 6.3, created 2025-09-09), not a browser capture. B02B: the decisive authority for the CPP2 deduction/credit split. Part 4 line 14 sends base(9.9%) + first(2%) + second(8%) additional contributions to line 42100 as payable; line 15 sends 50% of the BASE contribution only to line 31000 as the credit; line 17 sends that 50% plus ALL first and second additional contributions to line 22200 as the deduction — the second additional contribution is fully deductible and earns no credit. Nine split rates/maxima authored as CALC_CONSTANT (base 4.95%/9.9%, first additional 1%/2%, SE second additional 8%, and the four maxima); nothing already governed re-authored. The 83.1933% box-16 split factor was reviewed and REMOVED from the staged pack: Schedule 8 prints it only as a worksheet operand and it is 4.95/5.95 rounded — a derivable decomposition factor, not a published reference parameter (DERIVED_IMPLEMENTATION_CONVENIENCE); its citation remains as provenance. The treatment itself is NOT authored as a rule/formula — Part 4 arithmetic is the calculation TaxEngineService owns, and a parallel formula would be a second runtime authority. Measured against the engine read-only: payable identical; the engine's 50/50 split of the COMBINED total misallocates half of the first+second additional from deduction to credit (PRODUCTION_DEFECT, up to $1,074.00 misallocated and $108.48 total-payable overstatement in measured 2025 ON cases; not fixed in this ingestion run). CLOSES the CPP2_DEDUCTION_CREDIT corpus gap

files.internal_title: When to register for and start charging the GST/HST
files.note: When to register for and start charging the GST/HST, modified 2026-06-16. B13: GST_SMALL_SUPPLIER_THRESHOLD 30000 CAD authored for 2026 from the most-businesses table; RC4022 states the identical figure. The three temporal tests the table defines — a single-calendar-quarter test, a four-consecutive-calendar-quarter test, and cessation at the end of the month following the crossing quarter — are NOT authored: they measure worldwide taxable-supply revenue BEFORE expenses, including associates, per calendar quarter, and no fact measures taxable supplies at all, let alone by quarter; collapsing them into an annual net-income predicate would author a different rule than the source states. The event-relative timing (effective date no later than the crossing supply; register within 29 days) and the taxi/ride-share must-register-regardless carve-out are likewise blocked: deadlines carry only fixed dates as children of a rule version, and no occupation fact exists. The 50,000 and 250,000 public-service-body/charity figures are extracted and recorded, not authored — out of product scope
